title: Easy Lemon Herb Salmon Sheet Pan Dinner (40-Minute Family Meal)
contentHtml:
This lemon herb salmon sheet pan dinner gives you the whole meal on one pan: flaky salmon, crispy-edged potatoes, asparagus and roasted peppers with garlic, lemon and herbs. It looks like you tried harder than you did, which is exactly the kind of weeknight win we are after.

Servings: 6  |  Prep: 10 minutes  |  Cook: 30 minutes  |  Total: about 40 minutes

Why This Dinner Works

  • One pan: the protein, potatoes and vegetables all finish together.
  • Family-sized: written for six servings without requiring three different skillets.
  • Simple flavor: lemon, garlic and dried herbs do most of the work.
  • Easy cleanup: line the pan and dinner cleanup is basically handled.

Ingredients

  • 6 salmon fillets, about 5 to 6 ounces each
  • 2 pounds baby potatoes, quartered
  • 1 pound asparagus, woody ends trimmed
  • 2 red bell peppers, sliced into thick strips
  • 4 tablespoons olive oil, divided
  • 4 cloves garlic, minced
  • 1 lemon, zested and juiced, plus extra wedges for serving
  • 1 1/2 teaspoons dried oregano
  • 1 teaspoon dried thyme
  • 1 teaspoon garlic powder
  • 1 1/2 teaspoons kosher salt, divided
  • 3/4 teaspoon black pepper, divided
  • 2 tablespoons chopped fresh parsley, optional

Instructions

  1. Heat the oven. Preheat the oven to 425°F. Line a large rimmed sheet pan with parchment paper or foil.
  2. Start the potatoes. Toss the potatoes with 2 tablespoons olive oil, half of the minced garlic, 1/2 teaspoon oregano, 1/2 teaspoon thyme, 3/4 teaspoon salt and 1/4 teaspoon black pepper. Spread them cut-side down and roast for 15 minutes.
  3. Season the salmon. While the potatoes roast, mix 1 tablespoon olive oil with the remaining garlic, remaining oregano and thyme, garlic powder, lemon zest, half of the lemon juice, 1/2 teaspoon salt and 1/4 teaspoon pepper. Rub the mixture over the salmon.
  4. Add the vegetables. Toss the asparagus and bell peppers with the remaining tablespoon of olive oil, 1/4 teaspoon salt and the remaining pepper. Pull the pan from the oven, move the potatoes toward the edges and add the vegetables.
  5. Add the salmon. Place the salmon fillets in the open space on the sheet pan. Drizzle the remaining lemon juice over the salmon.
  6. Finish roasting. Return the pan to the oven for 12 to 15 minutes, or until the salmon flakes easily and reaches 145°F in the thickest part and the potatoes are tender.
  7. Serve. Sprinkle with parsley if using and serve with extra lemon wedges.

Dad-Proof Tips

  • If the potatoes are bigger than a golf ball, cut them smaller. Big chunks are how you end up waiting on potatoes while everyone stares at you.
  • Keep the salmon pieces close to the same thickness so they finish at roughly the same time.
  • Use the biggest sheet pan you own. Crowding everything together makes the vegetables steam instead of roast.
  • An instant-read thermometer removes the guesswork from salmon completely.

Easy Swaps

  • Use green beans or broccoli instead of asparagus.
  • Swap the red peppers for zucchini or sliced red onion.
  • Use Cajun seasoning instead of oregano and thyme if your family likes more kick.
  • No fresh parsley? Skip it. Dinner will survive.

Storage and Reheating

Refrigerate leftovers in a covered container for up to 3 days. Reheat the potatoes and vegetables in an oven or air fryer for better texture, and warm the salmon gently so it does not dry out.

This is an original The Man That Cooks Sometimes recipe built for a normal weeknight when you want dinner to look impressive without making it complicated.
